html_source: Stephen’s tenacious argument against the validity of fatherhood can be read as a gloss on the saying “It’s a wise child that knows its own father”, quoted both in Act 2, scene 2 of The Merchant of Venice, and in Samuel Butler’s translation of Homer’s Odyssey. If Stephen is applying the saying to his relationship with his own father, this might imply he suspects his mother of infidelity.
